This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

Why the F-14 Tomcat changed everything. In the 1960s, the US Navy faced a problem—their F-4 Phantom II couldn't match new Soviet threats. Faster bombers, longer-range missiles, and the specter of naval combat demanded something revolutionary. In 1970, Grumman delivered the F-14 Tomcat: an aircraft unlike anything else in the sky. Variable sweep wings that adjusted in real-time for speed and altitude. A massive radar system designed to track entire formations at once. A weapons load built on one terrifying idea: kill the enemy before they ever get close. The Tomcat wasn't designed to dogfight. It was designed to dominate. Watch those iconic wings sweep back and understand why this aircraft still looks like the future.
